How to Make a Layered 3D-Printed Plaque from an Image

Trace PNG or JPG artwork into solid colors, choose relief heights, and print a layered plaque using STL or multicolor 3MF.

Open Plaque Maker

1. Choose and trace your artwork

Upload a PNG or JPG, or try the built-in sample. A logo or illustration with distinct solid colors makes it easier to separate the design into tiers. Use Remove edge background if the background should stay outside the plaque. Check the traced colors and use Trace artwork after changing trace settings.

2. Set the size and order the color tiers

Enter the requested width. Tall designs scale down proportionally to stay within 240 mm high. The bottom row marked Base is the backing. Move a color upward to raise it and use the height fields to set the top of each tier measured from the print bed. For example, top heights of 2, 4, and 6 mm make three 2 mm tiers.

3. Build and inspect the preview

Select Build plaque and rotate the preview. Check the underside and edges, then inspect lettering and fine details. If small fragments remain, try stronger relief cleanup. If a detail is lost, try increasing the print size or adjusting the color trace.

4. Download and slice flat on the bed

Use Download 3MF for a project with assigned colors, or download the free STL tiers. Import all STL tiers together as parts of one object to retain their vertical offsets. In your slicer, keep the backing flat on the build plate and check the layer preview for gaps or unexpected supports before printing.
